I am developing accessible, practical learning resources that help students **reason with statistics**, not just perform calculations. The first collection is an Elementary Statistics course hub built around examples from psychology, behavioral health, and everyday research.

## Interactive resources in development

The first resource collection is based on the proposed course sequence. These are planned activities, **not active links to completed simulations**.

| Proposed topic | Course week | Intended activity |
|---|---:|---|
| Exploring distributions | 3–4 | Compare the mean, median, variability, and effects of outliers |
| Sampling distributions and central limit theorem | 6 | Repeat samples and explore how sample size affects the distribution of sample means |
| Confidence intervals | 7 | Examine repeated-sample interval coverage |
| Hypothesis testing and power | 8 | Investigate Type I/II errors, effect sizes, and power |
| Correlation and regression | 14–15 | Explore patterns, outliers, prediction, and limits of causal claims |

Each future lesson will be organized around a question, a prediction, an example or simulation, an interpretation task, and a short knowledge check. Interactivity will be used only when it improves understanding. Accessible explanations and alternatives will accompany required visual activities.

## Teaching approach

My instructional goal is to make statistical and research reasoning understandable and useful.

- **Begin with meaningful questions.** Connect statistical ideas to psychology, community mental health, and everyday evidence.
- **Build understanding gradually.** Combine clear explanations, worked examples, guided practice, and feedback.
- **Interpret before concluding.** Teach students to examine assumptions, bias, sampling, uncertainty, practical importance, and limitations.
- **Support different learners.** Use plain language, multiple ways to explain a concept, and accessible materials without requiring prior programming experience.

## Instruction and mentorship

Since 2016, I have contributed research and program evaluation instruction to the doctoral psychology internship training program at Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services.

Working with the internship training team, I guide approximately four doctoral interns annually through a yearlong research or program evaluation project. Instruction and feedback include literature review, study design, measurement, statistical analysis, interpretation, APA-style writing, and presentations. The work helps interns develop increasing independence as researchers and evaluators.

This instructional and mentorship experience is **distinct from a formal college teaching appointment**.

## Sample course design and related work

The Elementary Statistics materials draw from a **proposed PSYC 210 sample syllabus for Cerritos College**. It is not an active or officially approved class section; the approved course outline and departmental decisions would determine the final content and requirements.
